facts.text: Jordan Hill got its name around 1890 when Winn Parish superintendent Will Wallace noted the hilltop school and the Jordan family’s prominence.
The town’s heart is the Big Creek Baptist Church, founded in 1874 beside a stream and long serving as a hub for singing conventions and Sunday school.
Jordan Hill sits just east of the Dugdemona River and west of Kisatchie National Forest, where longleaf pine savannas and hardwood bottomlands shape local wildlife.
The community rises gently from 120 to 250 feet above sea level, creating a mix of upland ridges and floodplain wetlands that influence its small family farms.
A humid subtropical climate brings hot, humid summers averaging 93°F and mild winters that rarely drop below 35°F, with about 55 inches of rain each year.
After the Civil War, settlers like widower Eli Jordan claimed land under the Homestead Act, turning the hill country into a patchwork of 20‑to‑40‑acre family farms.
